mpc_20260417_184601.csv.notes: First session post-STANDBY refactor. Solver saturated (74.2% timeouts, max 440 consecutive = ~11s of 18.6s run). p50 solve 25.9ms > 24ms budget — typical solve over budget, not just peaks. Two cmd discontinuities at t=1.477s (leg 2: 10.5mm, leg 3: 9.4mm) at the moment ref stops moving — new/unknown pattern (MPC_FALLBACK_SAWTOOTH candidate). Trajectory was multi-axis (~40mm X + 50mm Y + 27mm Z combined), starting off-Active from unfinished command 4. act2 coasted 18mm past frozen cmd during 440-step hold before settling. LEG2_TRACKING known-issue match. HardwarePlant telemetry-stale E-STOP fired 108 times at t~11s — consequence, not cause. Rosbag confirms ACTIVE:STANDBY transition working as designed. Orchestrator refactor itself not implicated — saturation is the story.

mpc_20260417_151131.csv.notes: SPACEMOUSE mode via ROS2 pipeline (rosbag 2026-04-17_15-11-19 confirms ACTIVE:SPACEMOUSE at bag_t=3.8, mode=SPACEMOUSE at bag_t=6.1). 30.7% solver timeouts (184/600), max 178 CONSECUTIVE at t=0.9-6.6s during the initial z=170→189 ref jump. After 6s the solver clears completely (0 timeouts t=7-10s). p95 solve 30.4ms (was 19.7ms in 141354 static) — 54% regression vs last session. Tracking error grows during timeout burst (4.5mm → 26.8mm peak at t=7s), platform never catches ref (actual_z 211mm vs ref_z 220mm at final sample, 8.8mm pos error at end). No oscillation, 0 cmd_jumps (C1 fix still intact), no E-stop, no motor errors, clean state transitions. Root cause candidate: SpaceMouse-driven ref injects larger deviations than static-pose path → IPOPT blows CPU budget on bigger transients; 40ms tau may also be too fast for SpaceMouse step-like inputs. Rosbag shows orchestrator IDLE→ACTIVE:SPACEMOUSE→IDLE cleanly, so it's a planner-horizon-vs-CPU issue, not a plant/motor issue.
